name: XML Formatter
description: Pretty-print, minify or validate XML text.

results.outputHint: The result can be copied directly.

hints.input: Elements that contain text only stay inline: moving the text to the next line would insert whitespace into the content, which rewrites the data.
hints.action: Validate only reports whether the syntax is legal; it does not rewrite the content.
hints.indent: The indent width is measured in spaces; 2, 4 and 8 are available.
hints.keepComments: Comments are dropped by default; enabling the option keeps them near their original position.
hints.output: Format indents by depth; minify strips the whitespace between tags.

faq.a: No. The tool works token by token, so attributes are emitted in their original order.

faq.q: Why do text-only elements stay on one line?
faq.a: Whitespace inside an element is meaningful in XML. Splitting `1` across two lines turns it into `\n1\n`, which changes the content.
No. The tool only parses markup and text; it does not resolve DTD declarations or custom entities.
